name: Rosin
short: A solventless cannabis concentrate made by pressing flower, kief or hash with heat and pressure to squeeze out resin.
definition: Rosin is a concentrate made without chemical solvents. Producers place flower, dry-sifted kief or ice-water ('bubble') hash between heated plates and apply high pressure, which squeezes out a sticky resin rich in cannabinoids and terpenes. Pressing hash rather than flower usually gives a cleaner, more potent product. When the starting material is hash made from fresh-frozen plants, the result is sold as live rosin.

Solventless products appeal to consumers wary of residual chemicals and to small producers, because a press costs far less than a licensed hydrocarbon extraction lab and carries no risk of solvent explosions. A 2021 review in the Journal of Cannabis Research noted the trade-offs: heat helps yield but drives off terpenes, so equipment that achieves high pressure at lower temperatures preserves more aroma, and hash-making itself is labour-intensive and hard to scale.

Rosin commands premium prices in many US markets. Some states license solventless processing under a lighter category than solvent extraction, and in places where home grow is legal, small-scale rosin pressing is a common home activity, although making concentrates at home can be restricted or prohibited by state law.
example: Several small brands have built their reputations on solventless rosin pressed from their own harvests.
